glosses: A burden; a weight to be carried.

examples.text: I struggled up the hill with the heavy load in my rucksack.

glosses: A worry or concern to be endured, especially in the phrase a load off one's mind.

examples.text: Our life's a load.

glosses: A certain number of articles or quantity of material that can be transported or processed at one time.

examples.text: The truck overturned while carrying a full load of oil.
She put another load of clothes in the washing machine.

glosses: A quantity of washing put into a washing machine for a wash cycle.

examples.text: I put a load on before we left.

glosses: Used to form nouns that indicate a large quantity, often corresponding to the capacity of a vehicle
A large number or amount.

examples.text: I got loads of presents for my birthday!

glosses: The volume of work required to be performed.

examples.text: Will our web servers be able to cope with that load?

glosses: The force exerted on a structural component such as a beam, girder, cable etc.

examples.text: Each of the cross-members must withstand a tensile load of 1,000 newtons.

glosses: The electrical current or power delivered by a device.

examples.text: I'm worried that the load on that transformer will be too high.

glosses: A resistive force encountered by a prime mover when performing work.

examples.text: Connect a second 24-ohm load across the power supply's output terminals.

glosses: A unit of measure for various quantities.

examples.text: If this load equals its modern representative, it contains 18 cwt. of dry, 19 of new hay.

glosses: Ellipsis of viral load.

glosses: To be placed into storage or conveyance.

examples.text: The containers load quickly and easily.

glosses: To fill (a firearm or artillery) with munition.

examples.text: I pulled the trigger, but nothing happened. I had forgotten to load the gun.

glosses: To insert (an item or items) into an apparatus so as to ready it for operation, such as a reel of film into a camera, sheets of paper into a printer etc.

examples.text: Now that you've loaded the film [into the camera], you're ready to start shooting.
Now that you've loaded the camera [with film], you're ready to start shooting.

glosses: To fill (an apparatus) with raw material.

examples.text: The workers loaded the blast furnace with coke and ore.

glosses: To be put into use in an apparatus.

examples.text: The cartridge was designed to load easily.

glosses: To read (data or a program) from a storage medium into computer memory.

examples.text: Click OK to load the selected data.

glosses: To transfer from a storage medium into computer memory.

examples.text: The file took ten minutes to load.

examples.text: He walks to load the bases.

glosses: To tamper with so as to produce a biased outcome.

examples.text: You can load the dice in your favour by researching the company before your interview.

glosses: To ask or adapt a question so that it will be more likely to be answered in a certain way.
To encumber with something negative, to place as an encumbrance.

examples.text: The new owners had loaded the company with debt.

glosses: To provide in abundance.

examples.text: He loaded his system with carbs before the marathon.

examples.text: Il y avait chaque jour des troubles dans la rue. On brisait les kiosques et les sergents de ville chargeaient la foule.

— Dans leurs rangs éclata une furieuse colère : elles ne se sauvèrent pas, mais se jetèrent sur les cailloux et se mirent à bombarder les crânes de la cavalerie qui avait chargé.
